title: Heterogeneous superconductivity emerging from a charge-stripe state in kagome lattices
authors: Hongyu Li, Shuikang Yu, Huachen Rao, Zhuying Wang, Xingchen Zhou, Houpu Li, Yunmei Zhang, Zhao Gong, Xin Yu, Rui Wu, Tao Wu, Zhenyu Wang, Ziji Xiang, Xianhui Chen
abstract: Charge density wave (CDW) and superconductivity have long been recognized as competing orders. However, recent achievements establish that the interplay between these two collective electronic phenomena can be more perplexing, with emergent phenomena arising from their cooperation. Here we report a distinctive case of the kagome superconductors CsV3Sb5-xSnx, in which the characteristics of superconductivity evolve in accordance with the form of CDW order. As the triple-Q CDW in CsV3Sb5 transforms to a short-range stripelike CDW at xc = 0.07, a sudden change in superconducting properties occurs concomitantly. A combination of thermodynamic, electrical transport and scanning tunneling microscopy experiments reveals a heterogeneous superconducting state beyond xc: the superconducting gap exhibits pronounced spatial variation, in conformity with a distribution of critical temperature and the resulted superconducting precursor effects. Moreover, abundant normal fluid persists deep into the superconducting state, as evidenced by remnants of electronic specific heat and zero-energy quasiparticle interference. These observations are unrelated to the chemical inhomogeneity and residual strain effect introduced by Sn substitution. Instead, they emulate the phenomenology that a sign-changing superconducting order parameter is subject to strong pair-breaking scattering with the short-range charge stripes and hence reflect the unconventional nature of superconductivity developing inside the charge-stripe state.
summary: This work examines superconductivity in kagome superconductors where the CDW order changes. By combining STM and transport measurements, the authors reveal that the superconducting state becomes spatially heterogeneous when the CDW transitions to a short-range stripe pattern. This inhomogeneity is interpreted as evidence of unconventional superconductivity driven by pair-breaking scattering from the charge stripes.
main_problem: The paper investigates the complex interplay between Charge Density Wave (CDW) order and superconductivity in kagome superconductors, specifically how the superconducting state evolves as the CDW order changes.
main_result: The superconducting state in the stripe-ordered phase is found to be heterogeneous, attributed not to chemical disorder but to strong pair-breaking scattering from the short-range charge stripes, indicating unconventional superconductivity.
method: The study combines multiple experimental techniques, including thermodynamics, electrical transport measurements, and Scanning Tunneling Microscopy (STM) to probe real-space variations in the superconducting gap.
model_or_system: The system studied is the kagome superconductor CsV3Sb5-xSnx, which exhibits distinct CDW phases (long-range triple-Q, short-range stripelike, fluctuating) depending on the doping concentration x.
key_observables: Pronounced spatial variation of the superconducting gap ($\Delta$), distribution of critical temperature ($T_c$), superconducting precursor effects, and remnants of electronic specific heat.
important_parameters: Doping concentration x, which drives the transition between different CDW phases (e.g., at $x_c = 0.07$).
main_assumptions: The unusual superconducting signatures are assumed to arise from pair-breaking scattering by the short-range charge stripes, contrasting with simple BCS expectations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the phase diagram mapping CDW types vs. doping, and STM/transport data showing the disparity between different superconducting transition temperatures ($T_{c0}, T_d, T_{Tccs}$) in the stripe-ordered phase.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the competition between CDW and superconductivity, then uses transport and STM data to characterize the superconducting inhomogeneity in the stripe-ordered phase, and finally discusses the implications for the pairing symmetry.
why_interesting: The strong coupling between charge order (CDW) and superconductivity, leading to unconventional pairing mechanisms, is a central theme in strongly correlated electron physics, relevant to understanding high-Tc superconductors.
